document: Online Banking Simulation v1 — Business Requirements Document (DRAFT)
objectives: Deliver a coherent banking simulation using synthetic identities, accounts, balances, beneficiaries, and payments.
Demonstrate customer and bank-operations' journeys with role-based access and auditable state changes.
Build four agent families: BRD; technical design/coding/unit testing; system-test/automation; and defect root-cause analysis.
Make agent output reviewable, reproducible, schema-valid, source-linked, and subject to human approval.
Use security, privacy, accessibility, reliability, and testability as acceptance conditions — not optional polish.
Practice governance: baselines, versioning, change control, traceability, evidence, risk management, and retrospectives.
stakeholders: Architecture, Build & Unit Test / Development (Mohit & Team)

roles.name: Customer
roles.description: Registers, completes KYC, logs in, transfers and receives money, views and downloads statements.

roles.name: Bank operations
roles.description: Reviews KYC, activates/freezes accounts, views the audit trail; cannot initiate transfers.

in_scope: Customer on-boarding with KYC (Aadhaar, PAN) — Customer, Bank operations
Account on-boarding and activation — Customer, Bank operations

out_of_scope.reason: Not on the v1 build list
Format check only; verification against government or issuing-authority systems is mocked

assumptions: Aadhaar and PAN are the only KYC identifier types required for v1 onboarding.
Account balances, identities, and transactions are entirely synthetic; no integration with real banking rails or identity-verification providers is required.
'Login' and 'Logout' apply uniformly to both Customer and Bank operations roles unless a role-specific journey is later defined.
Minimum balance, daily transfer cap, and UAT ownership are unresolved and no default values are assumed until they are answered (see OQ-001, OQ-002, OQ-003).
The data-testid naming convention for automated testing is pending confirmation (OQ-004); these requirements do not depend on a specific convention.
Beneficiary management referenced in the charter's broader vision is deferred beyond v1, consistent with the scope agreement's exclusion.

requirements_functional.statement: The system shall allow a prospective customer to submit registration details including Aadhaar and PAN identifiers.
The system shall validate Aadhaar and PAN inputs against defined format rules and reject malformed values.
The system shall route a submitted KYC application to Bank operations for review.
Bank operations shall be able to approve or reject a KYC submission.
The system shall create an account record upon KYC approval, in a pending (not yet active) state.
Bank operations shall be able to activate a pending account.
Bank operations shall be able to freeze an active account.
The system shall allow Customer and Bank operations users to log in with valid credentials.
The system shall reject login attempts with invalid credentials.
The system shall allow an authenticated user to log out, terminating the session.
The system shall allow an authenticated Customer to initiate a money transfer from their own account to another account.
The system shall prevent Bank operations users from initiating money transfers.
The system shall debit the sender's synthetic balance and credit the recipient's synthetic balance upon a successful transfer.
The system shall record a transaction entry for every transfer, visible to both the sending and receiving Customer.
The system shall allow Customer and Bank operations users to view an account statement for a selected account and period.
The system shall allow a Customer to download their account statement as a file.
The system shall provide Bank operations with an audit-trail view of account and transaction state changes.

requirements_nonfunctional.statement: KYC and account data shall be protected with baseline security controls (e.g., encryption in transit, access control by role).
Customer PII (Aadhaar, PAN) shall be masked in UI displays and logs outside of authorized KYC review contexts.
Customer-facing screens shall meet baseline accessibility conformance (e.g., keyboard-navigable, labeled form fields).
Every state-changing action (KYC decision, account activation/freeze, transfer) shall be logged with actor, timestamp, and before/after state to support the audit trail.
Agent-generated pipeline artifacts (BRD, business rules, requirements) shall be schema-valid and source-linked to enable automated traceability checks.
Each in-scope customer journey (onboarding, login, transfer, statement) shall be reliable and testable such that it can be exercised end-to-end via automation.
